note: Attack vectors of 2022-2026 and the host condition each one needs, with the checks that look for that condition. Hand-written from public reporting; no vendor catalog is downloaded. Every check named here must exist in the catalog (the regression checks it).

attacks.name: ClickFix and FileFix paste-and-run lures
attacks.needs: the victim pastes a command into the Run dialog or the Explorer address bar; Windows keeps it in RunMRU / TypedPaths

attacks.name: Port forwarding for pivoting (netsh portproxy, as in CISA AA24-038A)
attacks.needs: a portproxy rule on a host that may reach the target segment

attacks.name: Infostealers reading the browser session store
attacks.needs: app-bound encryption turned off by policy, or the browser's debugging port opened

attacks.name: Malicious or hijacked browser extensions
attacks.needs: an extension with broad permissions, sideloaded or pulled from the store after the fact

attacks.name: Bring your own vulnerable driver (BYOVD)
attacks.needs: a signed vulnerable driver loadable, the Microsoft blocklist off, or test signing allowed

attacks.name: An application control policy used to stop the security agent (Krueger-style)
attacks.needs: a code integrity policy in force whose rules name the agent's binaries

attacks.name: Turning the antivirus off before the payload
attacks.needs: tamper protection off, broad exclusions, threats set to allow, or the service stopped

attacks.name: Event logging silenced so the intrusion leaves no trace
attacks.needs: the event log service or its autologgers stopped while the audit policy still reads as correct

attacks.name: LSASS credential dumping
attacks.needs: LSASS not a protected process, Credential Guard off or unlocked, WDigest storing clear text

attacks.name: Coercion and NTLM relay (PetitPotam and its successors)
attacks.needs: the WebClient service reachable, and SMB or LDAP accepting unsigned, unbound authentication

attacks.name: Name resolution poisoning with Responder or Inveigh
attacks.needs: LLMNR, NBT-NS, mDNS or WPAD still answering on the host

attacks.name: PrintNightmare and the driver install path
attacks.needs: Point and Print without the admin restriction, or a spooler running where nothing prints

attacks.name: Netlogon secure channel weakened (Zerologon family)
attacks.needs: signing, sealing or strong keys not required on the secure channel

attacks.name: Mark of the Web and installer protocol bypasses (Follina, ms-appinstaller)
attacks.needs: the zone marker stripped on copy, the App Installer protocol open, script types running on open

attacks.name: Tarrask hidden scheduled task
attacks.needs: a task whose registry entry has no security descriptor, so the Task Scheduler does not list it

attacks.name: A task or service parked among Windows' own
attacks.needs: an entry in a Microsoft folder created by someone else, or a service hook pointing elsewhere

attacks.name: WMI event subscription persistence
attacks.needs: a permanent consumer bound to a filter on the host

attacks.name: DLL load points inside trusted processes (AppInit, COR_PROFILER, IFEO, netsh, LSA, print monitors)
attacks.needs: a load point whose DLL is not Windows' own

attacks.name: DLL hijacking and planting in writable folders
attacks.needs: a program folder, PATH entry, service or task binary a non-administrator can write

attacks.name: Office macros through a trusted location
attacks.needs: a trusted location on a share or in a folder the user fills, or macros allowed with no signature

attacks.name: Updates taken over an unauthenticated channel (WSUS attack tooling)
attacks.needs: a WSUS server set by policy over http, or a user-level proxy in front of update detection

attacks.name: BitLocker bypass through the recovery environment
attacks.needs: a disk that unlocks itself (TPM only) with WinRE enabled and an unserviced recovery image

attacks.name: Remote monitoring tools used for hands-on-keyboard access
attacks.needs: a remote access or RMM tool installed, or RDP open with weak settings

attacks.name: OpenSSH on Windows as a way back in
attacks.needs: the OpenSSH server installed with keys in administrators_authorized_keys

attacks.name: BITS jobs that fetch and run the payload
attacks.needs: a BITS job with a notify command, retried by Windows for weeks

attacks.name: Logon screen and accessibility backdoors
attacks.needs: a replaced accessibility binary, an IFEO debugger on the logon tools, or a credential provider of someone else's

attacks.name: CredSSP and delegation abuse (CVE-2018-0886 and the delegation policies)
attacks.needs: unpatched CredSSP peers accepted, or credentials delegated to any server

attacks.name: SMBv1 and the EternalBlue family
attacks.needs: the SMBv1 server or its client driver still enabled

attacks.name: Reuse of a local account nobody watches
attacks.needs: an enabled local account unused for months, a shared local password, or no LAPS

attacks.name: Credentials left on disk and picked up later
attacks.needs: an answer file, a Group Policy Preferences password, PowerShell history or a saved credential

attacks.name: Ransomware clearing the way back (shadow copies, recovery, restore points)
attacks.needs: shadow copies disabled, or Controlled Folder Access and remote encryption protection off

attacks.name: Exploitation of a known vulnerability in installed software
attacks.needs: a product on the host with a published, exploited vulnerability, or one out of support

notCovered.name: Process injection and in-memory loaders
notCovered.why: runtime behaviour: nothing in a host's configuration shows it. The checks here only remove the conditions (application control, ASR, exploit protection); detection belongs to an EDR.

notCovered.name: Active Directory attack paths (Kerberoasting, delegation, AD CS templates, dMSA abuse)
notCovered.why: the evidence is in the directory, not on the host. HostBadger judges only what a member or a domain controller shows locally (signing, channel binding, RC4, DSRM).

notCovered.name: Server application vulnerabilities (Exchange, SharePoint, web stacks)
notCovered.why: they need the product's own state and logs. HostBadger sees the installed version, so software_cve and kev_software_match can place it, and nothing more.

notCovered.name: Secure Boot revocation state (bootkits of the BlackLotus family)
notCovered.why: the revocation list lives in a UEFI variable the collector does not read. secure_boot_off and boot_integrity_weakened say only whether Secure Boot and driver signing are on.

notCovered.name: Firmware and hardware implants, Kernel DMA attacks on an unlocked machine
notCovered.why: below the operating system. Only the policy side is judged (bitlocker_policy_gaps for the DMA setting, secure_boot_off, hvci_off).

notCovered.name: Phishing, consent phishing and anything that happens in the identity provider
notCovered.why: no local evidence. run_dialog_payload catches only the paste-and-run kind, once it reaches the host.

notCovered.name: Cloud and token theft after the host (session tokens, OAuth grants, device code flows)
notCovered.why: outside the host's configuration. browser_cookie_protection_off and credential_manager_saved cover the local store, not what was done with it.

notCovered.name: Supply chain compromise of a signed update
notCovered.why: a correctly signed package from the real vendor leaves nothing wrong on the host. trusted_publisher_added and root_ca_added catch only a certificate someone added locally.

notCovered.name: Hands-on-keyboard command execution as it happens
notCovered.why: HostBadger reads a snapshot, not a stream. It sees the command lines that persistence leaves behind (autostart_suspicious_command, run_dialog_payload), not the session.
